name: osce-pipeline-synthetic-cohort
description: Synthetic Korean OSCE patient cohort produced by a four-stage prompt-engineering pipeline. Each record is one fictional patient with chief complaint, ground-truth diagnosis, demographic + vital block, OSCE-style interview checklist, and a polished standardised-patient script. The bulk artefacts are generated locally from a closed reference corpus and are not redistributed in this repository — see the dataset_card and data/README.md.
citation: Yi Y, Park J, Kim S. A Stratified Multi-Rater Evaluation of LLM-Based Virtual Standardized Patients with a Deployed Data-Generation Platform. NeurIPS 2026, Track on Evaluations and Datasets.

rai:dataLimitations: Synthetic Korean OSCE patient records generated end-to-end by GPT-4.1 from a closed Korean medical-education reference corpus. Coverage and emphasis reflect what that corpus covers — expect over-representation of common undergraduate-OSCE conditions and under-representation of rare specialties. Korean-language only; English prompts ship as alternates but were not used in the released artefacts. Prompt outputs are not clinically verified.
rai:dataBiases: Korean-language origin and Korean medical-education curriculum. Disease distribution reflects the closed seed corpus, biased toward chief complaints emphasised in the 의사실기시험 (Korean OSCE) curriculum. Demographic distributions (age, gender) are LLM-imputed conditional on disease, so they reproduce LLM training-data priors rather than Korean population epidemiology.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: All patient records are fictional. No PHI; no real patient encounters. Patient names are LLM-generated and synthetic. The closed seed corpus is not redistributed in this repository.
rai:dataUseCases: Validity established for: training and evaluating LLM-based standardized-patient simulators, benchmarking automated OSCE checklist scoring, augmenting Korean medical-dialogue corpora. Validity NOT established for: clinical decision-making, diagnosis, evaluation in non-Korean contexts, or any standalone medical training without supervisory oversight.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Positive: lowers the cost of authoring OSCE practice materials and supports research on LLM-based clinical-skills tutors. Negative: LLM-generated patient personas may include plausible-but-clinically-marginal content; if mistaken for clinically validated material, downstream learners could be miscalibrated. Mitigations: explicit not-for-clinical-decision-making statement, verbatim prompt and decoding-parameter disclosure, sample-only repository release with full bulk artefacts gated.
rai:syntheticDataDescription: All four data-generation stages call gpt-4.1 (temperature=0.2, seed=42, no streaming): (1) per-symptom patient cohorts of 5 fictional patients each from a closed reference chapter, (2) merge into a single JSON tree, (3) OSCE-style 20+ item interview checklist per patient grounded in the same chapter, (4) two-step scenario authoring — a 2,000–2,500 character draft followed by a polish that spells out numerals, simplifies jargon, and breaks the text into 4–5 paragraphs voice-ready for a standardized-patient simulator. The full prompt set (4 data-gen + 5 runtime templates) is published verbatim under prompts/ in both Korean and English.
rai:wasDerivedFrom: A closed Korean medical-education reference corpus: one UTF-8 plain-text chapter per chief complaint, supplied locally by the authors. The corpus is not redistributed in this repository for copyright reasons; see data/README.md for the bring-your-own-corpus protocol.
rai:wasGeneratedBy: Pipeline: stages 1-4 in src/pipeline/, all using gpt-4.1 (temperature=0.2, seed=42) via langchain_openai.ChatOpenAI. Decoding configuration is verbatim in the source. Stage 4 fans out across patients with asyncio.gather (default --batch-size 5). Prompts are bilingual via the OSCE_LANG environment variable; the canonical experiment uses Korean. The runtime simulator and auto-grader (src/runtime/, src/grading.py) call gpt-4o (temperature=0 for structured tasks, 0.5 for chat; seed=42) — these are evaluation-time only and do not contribute to the synthetic patient cohort itself.
